counterfactual_missing_items: Specific DLBCL-defining features such as diffuse large-cell morphology and CD20/MUM1 subclassification are not explicitly stated
HHV8/EBV status is not reported, which would be needed to exclude primary effusion lymphoma
Histologic features of Castleman disease such as hyaline vascular or plasma cell changes are absent
decisive_items: Mix of small to large B lymphocytes
response.rationale: C1 uniquely integrates the diagnostic chylothorax (triglyceride 747 mg/dL) with biopsy-proven B-cell lymphoma (mixed B lymphocytes, aberrant BCL2, elevated Ki-67), covering both the effusion and its underlying cause. R3 captures only nonspecific aggressive B-cell lymphoma features and misses the chylothorax, while R4 confirms chylothorax but omits the lymphoma. R5, R2, and R6 are poorly supported by the immunophenotype and imaging.

rejected.why: Only supports pleural effusion; primary effusion lymphoma requires HHV8/EBV association and typically lacks a mass, whereas this case has mediastinal/hilar disease and BCL2-positive B-cell lymphoma.
The biopsy features are more consistent with a B-cell lymphoma than nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma; no LP-cell markers are provided and aberrant BCL2 with elevated Ki-67 is atypical.
Adenopathy alone is nonspecific; the biopsy shows B-cell lymphoma rather than Castleman disease histology and does not explain the chylothorax.
The triglyceride level confirms chylothorax, but this candidate omits the biopsy-proven lymphoma that is the underlying cause.
